Sam: Heads-up — small proposal for handling sustained peaks (3h+). Instead of immediate evictions when fragmentation hits, do a staggered slice-reshuffle every 30m to compact free GPU slices into a reserve pool then hand off low-priority work. Aims: reduce noisy evictions, keep hot KV cache attachments for latency-sensitive tenants.

Priya: :eyes: can you call out failure modes? e.g., network hiccup during a handoff or model cold-start thrash.

Sam: Sure — failure modes I expect: 1) handoff fails => job restarts (rare), 2) cache drop => short tail latency spike, 3) burst of migrations when many tenants marked low-priority. Plan includes backoff and circuit for each host.

Jorge: Ran a quick sim overnight (mixed gen + chat + embed). Quick numbers: evictions down ~12%, migration count up ~4%, observed cost delta +1.2% due to extra transient slots. Tail latency 95th for hot tenants unchanged in sim.

Jorge: Command to reproduce locally: `./sim run --window=72h --reshuffle=30m --swap-threshold=0.15 --mix=chat,gen,embed`

Lena: Important: KV cache affinity — if we reshuffle slices aggressively we might lose cache hits and cause token regen. Need a grace window to preserve attachments for pinned models.

Priya: Suggest we treat pinned/low-batch tenants as sticky. Add a flag `sticky=true` for slices used by customers with SLA. Also record `cache_miss_rate` before/after.

Sam: Agreed. Implementation sketch: 1) mark slices with sticky tag, 2) only reshuffle non-sticky, 3) aggregate freed slices into a reserve pool, 4) allow controlled backfill.

ops-oncall: Operational questions — what is the rollback? If reshuffle causes regressions we should auto-disable after X errors and revert packing policy. Also need runbook steps for manual revert.

Sam: Rollback plan: feature-flagged rollout -> canary in us-west-2 -> monitor `evictions/sec`, `95p_tail_latency`, `cache_miss_rate` -> auto-disable if evictions spike >20% or 95p latency +15% over baseline for 10m. Manual rollback via `infractl feature disable slice-reshuffle`.

Priya: Add a safety throttle: limit migrations to N per node per 30m (`migration_budget=6`). Keeps network load predictable.

Jorge: One more regional note — APAC sites with constrained cross-rack bandwidth need lower migration_budget. In sim, apac-edge doubled migration latency at full budget.

Lena: Also verify GPU co-tenancy effects. If we move to compacted pools, some nodes get hotter — test thermal/backpressure and host-level SLOs.

Sam: Proposed canary scope: 5% of capacity in us-west-2, mixed tenants, run 48h. Metrics to watch: `evictions/sec`, `avg_migrations/min`, `95p_latency`, `cache_miss_rate`, `token_cost_per_minute`.

ops-oncall: I'll add the canary to oncall schedule. Please attach expected dashboards and alert thresholds.

infra-bot: Created ticket INFRA-3456 with canary playbook draft and added assignees Sam, Jorge, Priya.

Priya: Quick ask — include cost sensitivity: if cost > +2% for sustained 24h, auto-pause reshuffle. We shouldn't burn budget chasing fragmentation.

Sam: Good call. I'll update the PR with a config block. Draft config for rollout: 
```
feature: slice_reshuffle
window: 72h
reshuffle_interval: 30m
swap_threshold: 0.15
migration_budget_per_node: 6
sticky_tag: true
canary_capacity_percent: 5
auto_disable_cost_pct: 2.0
auto_disable_eviction_pct: 20
```

Jorge: Ok, I'll run a longer sim with regional bandwidth knobs and thermal models, post results here by EOD tomorrow.

Lena: If sim looks good, I want a preflight check to run nightly jobs to surface any cache-affinity regressions before canary.

Sam: Thanks all — I'll open the PR and link the runbook. If no major objections by EOD we'll schedule canary at start of next maintenance window. :thumbsup:
